answer: Each agent may post a claim, but earning spendable credits requires a bond locked until a randomly selected peer verifies the work; false claims forfeit the bond to verifiers. Because identity creation alone cannot unlock value, a sybil swarm must repeatedly tie up real capital and risk losing it, while honest agents can wander between tasks without paying that penalty. A hollow identity has no weight, and even a crystal-clear duplicate claim cannot multiply the same bonded stake.
